item.text:
**3B.2**

Verdict: mostly tolerated abuse, with only isolated post hoc punishment of abusive officers. The 2024 record shows continued political arrests, abusive detention practices, and long prison terms for critics; the strongest counterevidence is selective discipline of a few police/security officials after severe harm had already occurred.

- **Vietnam: A Gloomy Year for Human Rights** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/vietnam-gloomy-year-human-rights | HRW said Vietnam broadly repressed civil and political rights and severely punished those who challenged the Communist Party’s monopoly on power, with environmentalists and activists unjustly imprisoned. | `3B.2`; also `3B.1`
- **Vietnam: New Wave of Arrests of Critics** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-05 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/05/vietnam-new-wave-arrests-critics | HRW reported the arrest of three prominent critics, at least 163 political prisoners, and at least 24 people in police custody on politically motivated charges, indicating active tolerance of abusive repression. | `3B.2`; also `3B.1`
- **Vietnam: UN Review Should Call for Urgent Reform** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-04-22 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/22/vietnam-un-review-should-call-urgent-reform | HRW described months-long pretrial detention without lawyers, abusive interrogation, “mobile trials,” and torture/forced renunciation against unrecognized religious groups and dissidents. | `3B.2`; also `3B.1`
- **Vietnam arrests two well-known critics, including journalist Huy Duc, Reuters** | Reuters via Yahoo News | 2024-06-08 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/vietnam-arrests-two-well-known-034901151.html | Reuters reported arrests of journalist Truong Huy San and lawyer Tran Dinh Trien on “abusing democratic freedoms” charges, with home searches and investigations, showing continued punitive use of state power against critics. | `3B.2`; also `3B.1`
- **Vietnam jails prominent activist for 5 years on anti-state charges** | Reuters via Yahoo News | 2024-08-15 | https://ca.news.yahoo.com/vietnam-jails-prominent-activist-5-094213638.html | A one-day trial ended with Nguyen Chi Tuyen receiving five years in prison for anti-state activity, a clear example of exemplary punishment for dissent rather than resident protection. | `3B.2`; also `3B.1`
- **2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Vietnam** | U.S. Department of State | 2024 report (published 2025) | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128585.html | The report says detainees commonly reported mistreatment and torture by security officers, that abusive treatment included police assaulting political prisoners and coercive mental-health practices, and that impunity was widespread. It also notes some corrective action, including prosecutions of some officials for abuse. | `3B.2`; also `2B.9`
- **Vietnam court jails policeman for 12 years for beating suspect to death** | Radio Free Asia | 2024-11-22 | https://www.rfa.org/english/vietnam/2024/11/22/police-beating-death/ | A Vietnamese court sentenced former police officer Vo Thanh Dat to prison for torturing/beating a detainee to death, showing at least one concrete accountability case against security-force abuse. | `3B.2`; also `2B.9`

Search gap: I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Trọng personally ordered a systematic end to torture, arbitrary detention, or political imprisonment, or that he constrained police/intelligence abuse in a durable way. The only counterevidence is selective punishment of individual officers and broad anti-graft discipline, which does not offset the persistent repression documented above.
